candidate.blueprint_topic: Management of Care — continuity of care, referrals, discharge barriers and resources
candidate.educational_objective: Recognize housing instability and transportation barriers as social determinants that can limit healthcare access and affect outcomes during discharge planning.

options.A: Address the housing issue only if it directly prevents medication storage, while treating transportation mainly as a scheduling inconvenience.
options.B: Recognize both as social determinants of health that can affect access to care and health outcomes after discharge.
options.C: Classify both barriers primarily as health-literacy problems even though the client understands the written plan.
options.D: Treat the barriers mainly as payer-authorization issues rather than factors that can affect the client's ability to carry out the discharge plan.

candidate.rationale: Healthy People 2030 defines social determinants of health as conditions in the environments where people live and identifies safe housing and transportation as examples. Its access-to-health-services literature summary states that unreliable transportation can interfere with consistent access to care and may contribute to negative health outcomes, while its housing-instability summary explains that unstable housing can negatively affect health and make healthcare access more difficult. These barriers therefore remain clinically relevant even when the client understands the medication instructions.
candidate.source_claim_supported: Healthy People 2030 identifies housing and transportation as SDOH; unreliable transportation may interfere with access to care and contribute to negative outcomes, and housing instability can negatively affect health and make healthcare access more difficult.
candidate.source_document_title: Healthy People 2030 — Social Determinants of Health; Access to Health Services; Housing Instability
candidate.source_locator: Social Determinants of Health → definition/examples; Access to Health Services → Literature Summary, transportation barriers; Housing Instability → Literature Summary, health and healthcare-access effects.
candidate.source_organization: U.S. Department of Health and Human Services, Office of Disease Prevention and Health Promotion (ODPHP)
candidate.source_version_date: Healthy People 2030 current federal framework; current pages rechecked 2026-08-16
candidate.stem: A client is medically stable for discharge and understands the medication plan but has unstable housing and unreliable transportation to follow-up visits. Which interpretation best explains why these barriers remain clinically relevant?
